# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

# [ms] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:1b1a9a4f943f⟧
Mode: Code Development (code)

Legend: 🎯session ●bugfix ◆feature ↻refactor ✓change ○discovery ⚖decision ⚠security_alert ⚷security_note ⊘sensitive
Format: ID TIME TYPE TITLE
Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 3 obs (1,305t read) | 27,912t work | 95% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
4 3:49a ○ ms unit parsing is a regex alternation plus a lowercase switch, with no microsecond support yet
5 " ○ parse tests use Jest describe/it blocks against parse() from ./index, with the README documenting casing and spacing rules
6 " ◆ ms() now parses microsecond units (us, µs, microsecond, microseconds) as fractional milliseconds
S3 Add microsecond support to ms(): accept `us`, `µs`, `microsecond` and `microseconds` as units so `ms("500us")` returns 0.5, updating the unit types, the README unit list, and adding tests. (Nov 3, 3:49 AM)
**Investigated**: Read src/index.ts (unit constants, Unit type unions, parse regex and switch, format functions), the README unit section and examples, and src/parse.test.ts (Jest describe/it conventions). Confirmed the parse regex is case-insensitive and anchored, and that the switch's `satisfies never` check forces type and switch updates to stay in sync.

**Learned**: Unit parsing has three coupled parts: the regex unit alternation, the per-unit type unions that feed the exported StringValue type, and the exhaustive switch in parse. The millisecond branch returns the raw number, so microseconds must divide by 1000 to yield fractional milliseconds. The README documents casing and spacing rules, and those are enforced at the type level only through parseStrict.

**Completed**: Parsing in src/index.ts now accepts the four microsecond aliases and divides by 1000, so `500us` gives 0.5 and `500US` works case-insensitively. A `Microseconds` type was added to the `Unit` union. The README unit list includes `Microseconds`, and a `ms('500us')   // 0.5` example was added near the top. A new test in src/parse.test.ts covers `500us`, `500 µs`, `1500 microseconds`, `1 microsecond`, `500US`, and `-500us`. The full Jest run passed with 168 of 168 tests and 100% coverage, and `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check src` were clean. The primary session reported that formatting is unchanged, so `ms(0.5)` still returns "0.5ms", and that nothing was committed.

**Next Steps**: The feature is implemented and verified. The session is idle, awaiting any further request.

**Notes**: The README example line was re-aligned after insertion, with a minor spacing tweak to the comment column. No new unit behavior was introduced beyond the requested aliases.


Access 28k tokens of past work via get_observations([IDs]) or mem-search skill.
